html:
The Yorta Yorta are an Aboriginal people of the country around the junction of the Goulburn and Murray rivers, in what is now northeast Victoria and southern New South Wales, around Echuca, Shepparton and the Barmah forest.

The river red gum forests and wetlands gave fish, waterbirds and plant foods. Neighbours included the Taungurung to the south, the Wiradjuri to the north and the Baraba Baraba to the west. Squatters took up their land from the late 1830s.

In the 1900s the Yorta Yorta became leaders in the fight for Aboriginal rights:

  • Many lived at Cummeragunja mission on the Murray. William Cooper, a Yorta Yorta man, founded the Australian Aborigines' League in the 1930s and in 1938 led a protest to the German consulate in Melbourne against the Nazi attacks on Jews.
  • In 1939 residents protested against conditions at the mission in the Cummeragunja walk-off.
  • In 2002 the High Court finally rejected their native title claim. The trial judge had found that the tide of history had washed away their traditional laws and customs.

See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Yorta Yorta are an Aboriginal people of the country around the junction of the Goulburn and Murray rivers, in what is now northeast Victoria and southern New South Wales, around Echuca, Shepparton and the Barmah forest.
